encodes: A complete ERC-6492 wrapper (non-zero factory, non-empty calldata) whose factory is not allowlisted: the deployment path is not open, so the payment must be refused.
provenance: x402-foundation/x402 pull request 3925, specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_evm.md at commit d0dcbf42 (not merged): "If authorization.from has no code and the signature ends with the ERC-6492 magic suffix, a verifier MUST accept it only through the deployment path ... and MUST NOT remove the wrapper and check the inner signature with ecrecover, whether or not the wrapper carries deployment data."
ERC-6492: the suffix check happens before ecrecover, so a counterfactual contract signature is never verified as if it were an EOA signature.

Measured by robertolocatelli81-dev on 26 October 2026 (x402 pull request 3925, comment 6425457514) with the three reference facilitators at be54b7d: for a payer without code and a valid low-s signature in an incomplete wrapper, TypeScript rejects, Go and Python verify it as valid.
Measured by us on 26 October 2026 with the verifier before this change: every wrapped form was rejected as SIGNER_MISMATCH, a rejection for the wrong reason, because the wrapper was not recognized.
description: The baseline authorization wrapped with a non-zero factory and non-empty calldata, for a payer without code, with an empty factory allowlist.
limits: This is a proposal and not a published vector. The reason codes ERC6492_NO_DEPLOYMENT_PATH and ERC6492_FACTORY_NOT_ALLOWED are ours, the published vocabulary has no code for a wrapped signature.
The text it follows is not merged. If the text changes, this vector moves with it.
A wrapper with an allowlisted factory and deployment data cannot be judged offline, it needs a simulation that deploys the wallet and makes the transfer together, so there is no vector for it here.
